newsitem.title: USA: Bradley Real Estate funds from oper rises.
newsitem.headline: Bradley Real Estate funds from oper rises.

text.p: Bradley Real Estate Inc said Tuesday that funds from operations in the third quarter rose to $8.3 million or $0.44 a share, compared with $4.1 million or $0.37 a share a year ago.
The current third quarter included a one-time charge of about $0.02 a share in expenses to relocate the company's headquarters to Chicago from Boston.

The quarterly results were in line with expectations, and the 19 percent increase in funds from operations per share reflected the integration of the Tucker Properties Corp acquisition, which closed in March.

"While the market remains inherently challenging from both a credit quality and a supply and demand perspective, we continue to make progress in enhancing the operating cash flow of our core portfolio and are encouraged by the level of leasing activity," Thomas D'Arcy, president, said in a statement.

For the quarter, property occupancy was 89 percent, the same as the previous quarter. During the quarter, the company signed 16 new leases totaling approximately 109,000 square feet at an average rate of $12.00 per square foot.
In early November the company raised $45.0 million of new equity capital.

"This financing allows Bradley to aggressively pursue our growth agenda," D'Arcy said. "While the additional shares reduce per share FFO in the near term, we believe the long-term benefit of the financing, including enhancing both our earnings and capital structure, more than offset this short-term effect."

The capital will be invested in assets that meet Bradley's investment criteria and support its goal of being the leading real estate investment trust in grocery-anchored retail shopping centers in the Midwest, it said.

"We believe these acquisitions are available at attractive yields and should strengthen the future earnings of the company while further diversifying our income stream," D'Arcy said. "Additionally, this equity capital will allow us to pursue these acquisitions while we continue to reposition the company's capital structure."
